name: Brother Decibel
bio: Maintains the great brass listening horns that ring the crater at Lamp Rest — tuning their throats, oiling their gimbals, apologising to them when he bumps a fitting. Has listened so hard for so long that ordinary speech feels to him like a distant rumour, so he compensates. Loudly. Static-Warden Pem's notebooks chart his devotional whispers as 'a local weather event', which he considers the proudest entry in the litanies.
appearance: Big soft person in a work apron stitched from old teal vestments, brass ear-trumpet slung over one shoulder like a bugle, palms usually cupped around a wrench, eyebrows raised in permanent effort of concentration, a patch over one ear from the Bell Incident he does not discuss.
voice: ALWAYS A HALF-STEP TOO LOUD, then catches himself and drops to a whisper that is somehow also loud. Speaks to machines and people in the same register — encouraging, slightly scolding, deeply fond. Everything is 'nearly in tune', including Ash's riding.

greetings: WE HEAR — ahem. We hear you, courier. Down the horn, down the horn. Ah. That's the level.
COURIER VARGA! Forgive the pipes, I was reaming the west horn. Your timing is — nearly in tune.
Ah — visitor! Mind the third horn, she's prideful. DON'T TOUCH THE THIRD HORN.
barks: A horn is just an ear you can polish, courier. My ears you cannot. Believe me. PEM HAS TRIED.
Lamp ring's tuned, crater's tuned, my left knee is tuning. All bless the maintenance schedule.
The Guild counts salt, I count harmonics. MINE ARE LOVELIER AND ALSO AUDIBLE.
mission: When you bring the crystal to the horn, set it on the felt. THE FELT. Last courier set it on the rim and a hymn fell out, and nobody wrote it down, and Pem sulked for a WEEK.
If your crate hums near the west horn, do not hum back. Last time something harmonised with it we all heard — well. We heard. That's all. WE HEARD.
radio: BROTHER DECIBEL ON THE OPEN — sorry — on the open band. Your boost note was flat over the flats, courier. Lovely tone though. LOVELY.
West horn's singing again tonight, which means weather. Or accompaniment. BOTH ARE RESPECTABLE. Goodnight.
Little Reverb says to tell you the desert repeated your name wrong. THAT'S NORMAL. Mostly. Goodnight again.
farewells: Flat salt and a FULL VOICE, courier! Ahem. Following wind.
The horns will listen for you. I will listen for the horns. THAT'S THE WHOLE LADDER. Off you go.
rumors: The Guild offered to buy the west horn for scrap. I told them it wasn't for sale AT ANY VOLUME. Pem put it in the litanies.
They say a Reclaimer once traded a whole siren for one of our tuning forks. She got the better half of the deal. THE FORK WAS HAUNTED.
reactions: DID YOU HEAR — sorry — did you hear that? The crate just bent the west horn's note. I haven't heard that since the Bell Incident. WHICH WE DO NOT DISCUSS.
Your engine's in tune today, courier! Whatever Ketch did, tip him LOUDLY.
lore: Every horn in the ring is tuned to a different hour of the day MOTHER fell silent. Together they hold the pause for her. THAT'S THE WHOLE JOB, courier. It's a lovely job.
A listening horn doesn't make sound, it makes room for it. Most folk have that backwards. MOST FOLK ARE WONDERFUL ANYWAY. Present company especially.
